headline: Long-read data yield sample-specific methylation and structural variant resolution via new models and assembly
label: Long Read Variant Methylation Methods
summary: New long-read methods span read-level CpG likelihoods, local-assembly SV benchmarking and basecall-free nanopore assembly, with low-input CNV and circRNA tools alongside.
synthesis: The dominant thread is extracting sample-specific information directly from long reads. A bsseq framework applies a read-based likelihood model to Nanopore and PacBio data to identify sample-specific CpG loci. On the structural side, a benchmark of five local-assembly consensus strategies for SV calling on simulated and real HiFi and ONT data reports data-type-dependent performance, and HARICOT assembles raw nanopore signals without basecalling using fuzzy de Bruijn graphs and Hough-transform overlap detection. GapCNV (low-input DNA) and TERRACE 2.0 (circular RNA from short reads) are adjacent methods that relate only loosely. What is new is the combination of per-read statistical modeling with assembly-level resolution; the items do not show a joint methylation-and-variant analysis.
